# Process Sensor Anomaly Detection & Drift Monitoring Prototype

An unsupervised anomaly-detection and drift-monitoring prototype over
synthetic multivariate sensor streams, built to demonstrate the
model-development and model-reliability work described in industrial
ML roles: experiment design, model comparison on held-out data,
threshold calibration on clean data only, and drift monitoring with
explicit false-alert accounting.

**Built 2026-11-16. All data is synthetic** — generated by
`generate_data.py` from a fixed seed (42). Nothing here is real plant
data, spectral data, or chemistry/process-engineering content. Channel
names (temperature, pressure, flow, conductivity, vibration, valve)
are generic labels for numeric streams.

## What it does

1. **Generates** 30 days of 1-minute sensor readings: 43,200 points × 6
   channels, with operating phases (production / cleaning / changeover),
   daily + weekly cycles, AR(1) noise, and cross-channel coupling.
   The first 14 days are clean (reference window). Days 15–30 carry 62
   labeled injected faults (40 spikes, 8 stuck sensors, 8 level shifts,
   6 noise bursts; 3,290 fault points) and a gradual sensor drift from
   day 24 (+0.15σ/day on temperature and conductivity).
2. **Compares 4 unsupervised detectors** fit on the clean window only,
   on causal features (standardized channels + 15-minute rolling
   mean/std): rolling z-score baseline, Isolation Forest, One-Class
   SVM, Local Outlier Factor. Thresholds are calibrated at the
   train-window 99.5th percentile — no test labels are used for
   thresholding.
3. **Monitors drift** with PSI + Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests per channel
   on 6-hour windows, matched on operating phase and time of day, with
   a 3-consecutive-window persistence rule before an alert confirms.
4. **Serves** the best model (One-Class SVM) and drift checks via
   FastAPI (`/health`, `/score`, `/drift`).

## Measured results (from `./demo.sh`, deterministic, seed 42)

Anomaly detection, held-out 16-day test window (days 15–30):

| Method | F1 | Precision | Recall | ROC-AUC | Events detected | Median delay | False alarms/day |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| One-Class SVM | **0.785** | 0.797 | 0.774 | 0.968 | 62/62 | 0 min | 40.6 |
| LOF | 0.766 | 0.645 | 0.943 | 0.972 | 61/62 | 0 min | 106.8 |
| Isolation Forest | 0.159 | 0.566 | 0.093 | 0.848 | 18/62 | 8 min | 14.6 |
| Rolling z-score baseline | 0.034 | 0.671 | 0.017 | — | 52/62 | 0 min | 1.8 |

Pre-drift slice (days 15–23, before drift onset): One-Class SVM F1
0.834, LOF 0.825, Isolation Forest 0.123, baseline 0.030.

Definitions: precision/recall/F1 are point-level on labeled fault
points. "Events detected" counts an injected fault event as detected
if any of its points is flagged; "median delay" is minutes from event
start to the first flag inside the event (0 = flagged at the event's
first minute). False alarms/day counts flags on clean points.

Drift monitoring (PSI > 0.2 AND KS p < 0.01, 3-window persistence):

- 1 false confirmed alert across 36 pre-onset windows.
- First confirmed alert on a drifting channel 54 hours after onset
  (temperature); both drifting channels (temperature + conductivity)
  confirmed within 66 hours of onset and sustained through the end of
  the 30-day run (22 confirmed alerts / 64 windows total).

Honest notes on the numbers: Isolation Forest genuinely underperformed
here — the comparison is reported as measured, not tuned until every
method looked good. The z-score baseline catches event onsets (52/62)
but flags almost nothing inside long events because its rolling mean
adapts. LOF has the best recall and ROC-AUC but by far the highest
false-alarm rate. One-Class SVM was selected for the API on F1.

The drift monitor went through two real fixes, documented in
`drift.py`: (1) pooled-reference comparisons false-alarmed on regime
mix and time-of-day (35 pre-onset windows) → phase + time-of-day
matching; (2) single-window alerts still false-alarmed on weekly
wander and short faults (24 windows) → 3-window persistence rule.
The final numbers above are from the fixed version.

## Limits (read before citing this project)

- Synthetic data only, fixed seed. No real industrial, spectral, or
  chemometric data; no chemistry or process-engineering claims.
- Models are scikit-learn (no PyTorch/JAX/TensorFlow in this
  prototype). No Databricks, no streaming infrastructure, no
  on-device/edge deployment.
- The drift thresholds (PSI 0.2, KS p 0.01) and persistence rule are
  documented conventions, not tuned optima.
- The API scores whatever window it is sent; `/drift` expects a
  same-regime window compared against the production-phase reference.

## Run it

```
./demo.sh   # generate + evaluate + unit tests + live API smoke test
```

Requires the project virtualenv at `.venv` (scikit-learn, FastAPI,
uvicorn; NumPy/pandas/SciPy come from system site-packages). Re-running
produces identical metrics (fixed seed; verified by repeated runs).

## Files

- `generate_data.py` — synthetic stream generator + ground-truth labels
- `detect.py` — features, models, evaluation
- `drift.py` — PSI + KS drift monitor
- `api.py` — FastAPI service
- `run_evaluation.py` — end-to-end run, writes `report.json`
- `tests/test_project.py` — 9 unit tests (determinism, labels, PSI, report ranges)
- `report.json` / `sensor_data.csv` / `artifacts.pkl` — outputs of the last run
